kf: **Livedo reticularis** is a violaceous, net-like (reticulate) mottling of the skin from sluggish blood flow.
Physiological (cold, complete regular rings, fades on warming) versus pathological (**livedo racemosa**: broken, irregular, persistent).
Pathological causes: antiphospholipid syndrome, vasculitis (PAN), cholesterol emboli, cryoglobulins, calciphylaxis, drugs (amantadine).
Investigate persistent or broken livedo: FBC, clotting, antiphospholipid antibodies, ANA, cryoglobulins, renal function.

sub: Physiological cutis marmorata common in infants and young women.

myths: **"Mottled skin is always harmless"**: persistent, broken livedo may signal clotting or vasculitis.
patho_lead: Livedo appears when blood **pools in the venous network** at the edge of each skin perfusion cone.

mech.t: Each arteriole supplies a cone of skin; the edges are drained by a venous plexus.
Cold, spasm or blockage slows flow so deoxygenated blood pools at the cone edges: a violet net.
Patchy arteriolar blockage (thrombosis, vasculitis) breaks the rings into irregular shapes.

comp: Depends on cause: ulceration, stroke, renal failure.
prog: Physiological livedo is benign; pathological livedo follows its cause.
